Key growth drivers include China+1 sourcing, OBBBA, India’s cell manufacturing ramp-up, and growing global LFP adoption. The company targets 40,000 MTPA of LFP cathode capacity by FY28 (capex ~INR11.25b) and is developing anode materials through a 200 MTPA pilot facility (~INR1.2b investment).  Himadri acquired Birla Tyres for INR3.1b, enabling forward integration for its carbon black business. Production resumed at Balasore in May’25, leveraging in-house carbon black to improve control over tyre chemistry. With 49 distributors, 1,000+ dealers, and exports to seven countries, the company plans to expand its SKUs from 75 to ~400 and enter the PCR tyre segment in FY27. These initiatives are expected to drive 109% revenue CAGR over FY26–29.  Himadri is leveraging its leadership in CTP and integrated carbon platform to expand into higher-value specialty segments, including carbon black, carbon nanotubes (CNTs), super specialty carbon black (SSCB), and specialty chemicals. Rising demand from EVs, batteries, and electronics, along with China+1 sourcing opportunities, will lead to diversification and margin expansion.  We expect Himadri to deliver strong growth (24%/23%/21% CAGR in revenue/EBITDA/PAT over FY26–29), driven by the scaling of its battery materials, specialty carbon black, CNT, and SSCB businesses, alongside the expansion of Birla Tyres. We value the company at 30x FY29E EPS with a TP of INR780 and a BUY rating. Battery materials: Building capabilities for energy transition  Himadri is entering the lithium-ion battery materials space through LFP cathode active materials and anode materials. According to the Press Information Bureau, ~178 GWh of additional cell manufacturing capacity is expected over the next five years, taking India’s total cell capacity to ~181 GWh and implying ~USD7b battery materials opportunity. This could translate into ~2% market share for the company by FY30.  Further, Himadri targets ~USD3b revenue from battery chemicals in the next six years, implying ~2% global market share by FY35 (global market of USD193b). LFP cathode capacity is planned to scale from 2,000 MTPA in 3QFY27 to 40,000 MTPA by FY28, with ~INR11.25b capex. Anode development includes a 200 MTPA pilot facility (Apr’26) with ~INR1.2b capex.
